properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/31/2023 to SLT PRODUCTION LLC in Pleasant Township, Warren county. 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery.  Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SLT PRODUCTION LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/31/2023
Violation Code: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days.
Violation ID: 8154384
Permit API: 123-44864
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/31/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). At the time of inspection the operator has broke apart the 6-5/8"x1-1/2" annulus production line and vented it to atmosphere in an attempt to mitigate the methane that was previously detected at 15% methane by volume in a slam bar hole. 0psi was observed on the 1-1/2" pressure gauge and the 6-5/8"x1-1/2" annulus was venting to atmosphere. 1 slam bar hole was placed into the ground within 2' of the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. 15% Methane was detected in slam bar hole #1 utilizing a MSA ALTAIR 5X meter which was calibrated on 07/17/2023 possibly indicating methane is still escaping from the well, as a result the following violations will continue against this well. VIOLATION: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING – DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. VIOLATION:78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. VIOLATION: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING – GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times At this time the department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator. Further inspection may be warranted.

Report Details

Violation Date: 2019-07-11
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 855603
Permit API: 035-21316
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Chapman Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-07-11
Comments: I met with Shawn Gearhart of XTO when I arrived. Containment was being pulled up on the side of the pad closest to the entrance. I noted two distinct areas of stressed vegetation off the west side of the pad (see map), and soil conductance readings were elevated off the entire west side of the pad. Where the containment had been removed, I was able to get conductance readings in several puddles. Near where the blender had been during the frac, I found two puddles with elevated conductance (5.31 and 7.49 mS/cm, see map for location). Puddles on the north side of the pad showed low conductance (.79-1.2 mS/cm). No XTO EH&S representative was present on the site during my inspection. Outstanding violations from 7/5/19 inspection cited.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. All annuli were closed when I arrived w/ the exception of the 21HC (20x13) annulus and the 6H (9x5) annulus which were opened early.- Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. - The (20x13) annulus vent of the 21HC was opened within first 27 hrs. of SPBUT due to pressures exceeding 30 psi and the 6H (9x5) annulus vent was opened within 13.5 hrs. Comments: An Administrative Compliance Schedule Evaluation (CSE) is being conducted in regard to the Sproul well site in Stewart Township, Fayette County. The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025.The 12/16/2021 CO and A states that the operator "shall restore the Sproul 7005 Site in accordance with the restoration plan in the expired Sproul ESCGP, including but not limited to the installation of all Post Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices ("PCSM BMPs"). Restoration of the Sproul 7005 Well Site shall be completed by October 30, 2025." The operator shall then "submit a Notice of Termination ("NOT") for the Sproul ESCGP once permanent vegetation has been established at the Well Site in accordance with 25 Pa. Code 102.7. The NOT shall be submitted to the Department no later than December 31, 2025.A Notice of Termination (NOT) request was submitted to the Department by the operator on December 31, 2025. A notarized Post-Drilling Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration and the updated map requested in IR 4085078 were submitted with the operator's NOT request on December 31, 2025.The Department observed possible cracking and developing soil displacement on the slope north of the well pad during the time of IR 4119144. The operator reported on 1/16/2026 that they conducted repairs in this location and provided a photo of the repairs (IR 4128095). It appeared in the photo provided by the operator that the repair resulted in ground disturbances, as they applied temporary stabilization after completing their repairs. M4 has failed to restore the Well Site pursuant to the COA and First Amendment.A violation shall be issued in this inspection for failure to comply with the 5/01/2025 amendment of the 12/16/2021 CO and A.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: APEX ENERGY (PA) LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/25/2024
Violation Code: 78a64a(d) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT - Secondary containment failed to have storage capacity sufficient to hold the volume of the largest single aboveground primary containment, plus an additional 10% of volume for precipitation.
Violation ID: 8173126
Permit API: 129-28930
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Salem Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/25/2024
Comments: On January 25 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Fatur Well Pad after a Department OGI requested a follow up in regards to a pink oily substance observed on the pad.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The Act 9 sign was present at the time of the inspection, and appeared to be in good condition. The ERP and PPC plans were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head at the time of this inspection. There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible leaks. Upon inspection of the GPU, there appeared to be a red tinted fluid in the containment surrounding the GPU. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid with in the containment and revealed elevated readings of 4.39mS. Upon further inspection, there appeared to be a disconnected hose and red tinted fluid on the gravel behind the GPU. Conductivity readings were taken from the surface on the ground beneath the puddles on the well pad and indicated elevated readings of 1.08mS and 1.37mS in comparison to the background reading of 0.12 mS taken from the surface of the soil along the well site perimeter. Directly adjacent to the GPU was a container with red colored fluid labeled as gear lubricant. The Department recommends the operator assess the red tinted fluid observed on the ground near the GPU as well as inside of the containment and remediate any spills in accordance with Department standards. The Department requests clarification on what the red tinted fluid observed on the ground is and how much was released with in 10 days of receiving this report.Upon inspecting the additional production equipment onsite, there appeared to be oil based matter being absorbed by cloths beneath the compressor. There did not appear to be any staining on the ground surrounding the compressor. The Department recommends the operator ensure the structural integrity of the all production equipment is sound and properly contain and dispose of any production related fluid in the proper manner to prevent any future pollution events. Upon inspection of the area mentioned by an OGI to have a pink oily matter on the ground, it appeared that a majority of the substance may have been washed away by recent rain as only small spots of a pink colored matter was observed on the ground surrounding a production tank next to the compressor. Conductivity readings were taken on the ground where the pink substance was observed and did not indicate elevated reading with readings of 0.13mS and 0.11mS. Upon inspection of the production tank and containment, the pink oily fluid was observed. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid with in the containment and did not indicate elevated readings with a reading of 0.09mS. The Department requests information regarding what was released and how much was released in this area with in 10 days of receipt of this report. The Department recommends removing excess fluids from secondary containments in order to ensure they meet required holding capacities of 110% according to Chapter 78a64a.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the release observed near the GPU, failure to have the gear lubricant in proper secondary containment, and the secondary containment for the production tank near the compressor failing to meet proper storage capacity. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of operator response.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: WILMOTH INTERESTS INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/23/2025
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8253359
Permit API: 123-48915
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sheffield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/23/2025
Comments: A production equipment malfunction at the ANF 194 49 conventional well resulted in a release of crude oil and produced fluids. The Department was notified of the release by Jason Wells of Wilmoth Interests, Inc. The well was shut in from the gathering lines at the time of the malfunction. Therefore, when the malfunction occurred, downhole pressure released vertically from the well head causing crude oil to be sprayed a significant distance above the well before ultimately settling on the well pad and nearby vegetation. The approximate radius of crude oil laden vegetation and forest understory spans 200 feet in every direction from the well head. It appears that the heaviest aerial migration of the release traveled in a southeast to easterly direction from the well. The exact volume of the release is not immediately quantifiable, but it is clearly in excess of the one barrel limit set forth in the Department's spill policy.The bulk of the fluids released settled on the well pad. At the time of this inspection, 3-4 inches of crude oil and produced fluids were present on the pad near the well head. Recent rainfall contributed to the volume of liquid present on the pad, and some stormwater runoff was observed to be flowing down the access road berm and onto the pad. The specific conductance of standing fluid on the pad near the flow of stormwater was found to be 6,080 micro Siemens per centimeter. The specific conductance of standing fluid near the well head was found to be in excess of 20,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. No fluids with elevated specific conductance were observed beyond the well pad at the time of this inspection.The crude oil released on the well pad was observed to have migrated beyond the well pad and downslope in a southern direction. The brush barrier downslope of the well pad was heavily coated with crude oil. Pooled crude oil was observed to have migrated beyond the brush barrier on the forest floor and potentially via porous subsurface material. The extent of pooled crude oil visible on the surface of the forest floor was located at a point approximately 180 feet south/southeast of the well pad.Cleanup efforts began immediately after the release was discovered and brought under control. A ditch was excavated along the downslope end of the well pad to provide containment and a means by which to collect pooled fluids with a vac truck. Jason Wells contacted a consulting firm soon after the release with the intent to retain a consultant to oversee the cleanup process for Wilmoth. I spoke with Jason onsite at the time of this inspection to notify him that violations would be included with the inspection report.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: This unconventional well is currently housed within a cellar (onto which a well tag has been affixed) and appears to be shut in. There is no infrastructure or equipment on the well site that would indicate that the well is (or has ever been) able to be produced. This well was spud on 8/18/2011, all submitted production reports for this well since that time indicate that the well has not been produced. The Department does not appear to have received a well log/record or completion report for this well. There is a second well (047-24582) on this pad, which was plugged in August of 2013. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0022 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling of this well and the plugging of 047-24582. The site ID sign for this well site is located at the end of the spur road that leads to this well. This sign does not meet the requirements of 78a.55(4). The access road leading to this well site is in suitable condition for the limited traffic that is currently using it. Maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road given its proximity to the West Branch of the Clarion River. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site and the access road banks appears to be established, future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site.

Comments On 3/7/17, Mr. Kepler with Seneca Resources contacted the Department regarding a small release of production fluid from a booster pump near the intersection of Middle Fork Road and Shawmut Grade Road. The pump is installed along a temporary water line running from Seneca's F10-F pad to their Clermont Storage Facility. The following was submitted to the Department in an email from Mr. Kepler: "The attached photo depicts the cracked head of a booster pump that was being used to move fluid from the F10-F flowback to the storage facility. An operator was on location when the incident occurred and the unit was immediately shut down and the isolation valves were closed. There were no injuries. A minimal amount of fluid was released as a spray, but the roadside ditch water associated with today's rain storms was impacted." The release was estimated to have lasted 15 seconds, releasing approximately 15-20 gallons of production fluid from Seneca's 047-24926 and 047 -24927 wells, both producing fluid at the time of the release. Upon inspection, soil conductivity readings were below 200 uS/cm along the ditch. The fluid released to the ditch had also been removed. The release constitutes violations of CSL 307(a), SWMA 301, and 78a57(a). These violations are being cited for both active wells that were producing fluid during the release. All violations will be resolved as they were immediately corrected. Failed to properly store/transport production fluid.

Additional violations are being issued against the accelerated erosion and heavy sedimentation observed in the access road.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/24/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 960283
Permit API: 081-21878
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/24/2022
Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the COP Tract 551-B pad. Inspection accompanied by EQT Lead EHS Coordinator Mark Barbier. Meeting on site with EQT Company Man Mike Hood. Weather conditions at time of inspection are partly cloudy, humid and 73 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while EQT reviews SOPs.According to the Standard Detail Report, the spill notification was submitted by Mr. Barbier. At around 0800 hours, US Well Services was swabbing the well to switch over from the 6H to the 7H well. At that time, the open topped blender hopper overflowed releasing an estimated 140 barrels of fluid to containment, of which an unknown quantity of fluid overtopped the containment structures. During discussions on site with Mr. Barbier, the estimation was based on the fact that the pumps may have been releasing 20 barrels per minute for 7 minutes, although the exact volume can not be determined. The Department conducted conductivity screenings using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Pooled fluid remaining within the containment structure was observed with conductivity readings between 7-8 mS/cm. Fluid within the north pad ditch and sumps outside of containment ranged from 3.92-5.37 mS/cm. Visual evidence of spilled fluid extended from a brushy area at the north conrer of the pad, along the entire ditch perimeter into the woods at the eastern corner of the pad where appeared to collect in a row of silt sock. Two vac trucks are present on site. One truck is vacuuming fluid from containment, a second truck is pumping spilled fluid collecting at he low point in the eastern corner of the pad ditch (photo 9). Visual observations near the blender unit indicated that fluid was released with sufficient force to release frac sand from the hopper. Two drums of frac sand were hand shoveled from the spill area (photo 10). Friction reducer material was also observed on pad rock outside containment. On the pad surface, spilled fluid is observed leaking through pad rock under the working tank secondary containment (photo 5). Pad rock affected by spilled fluid under containment is estimated to cover an area of 250 feet in length by 25-40 feet in width. The north ditch line channel is estimated at 400 feet in length with spilled fluid flowing an additional 25-50 feet off the north and east corners of the pad (photos 4 and 8). During discussions with Mr. Hood, when the well switch over occurs, down well fluid volumes are reduced and the blender valves must be adjusted to correspond to the reduced flow rate. Mr Hood indicated that the spill was caused by the blender operator falling asleep and failing to close a valve connecting the blender pumps to the working tanks during the well switch. Prior to site departure, Andy Steffee, Project Manager with Creston Environmental, arrived on site with a crew to begin conducting site characterization and sampling activity. Based on unknown volume of fluid spilled, Mr.Barbier indicated that EQT will immediately begin Act 2 remediation work. Well stimulation activity is expected to last into August at this location. Violations noted during this inspection and outstanding violations are extended.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/08/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 907794
Permit API: 129-24892
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Washington Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/08/2021
Comments: At the time of inspection, well appears to be equipped for production (Photo 1). Well label and tag present on well head (Photo 2). Pipe extending from brine tank appears to have a leak. The pipe appears to have significant rusting. The soil underneath the elbow joint of the pipe is saturated (Photos 3 and 4). Photo 5 show the underside of the pipe as it appears wet. The Department observed liquid dripping from the area shown. Two conductivity readings were taken from the saturated soil (Photos 6 and 7) showing readings of 6,410 microsiemens and 14,840 microsiemens. No background readings of the soil were recorded due to the ground being frozen everywhere excluding the affected area, however, due to the elevated readings of the affected area it appears that release is occurring. Photo 8 shows brine tank with well label present. Photo 9 shows the top of the brine tank lacking third-party protection. The Department recommends that the spill be remediated. The Department recommends the pipe be remediated or replaced. The Department recommends that the brine tank is protected against third-party acts. The Department requests inspection logs for the brine tank for the past 3 months. The Department requests information on how much fluid was lost and how the operator quantifies that information. The Department requests the waste manifest once it is available. The Department contacted both Lisa Raffle and Josh Martz of Diversified and notified them of the leak; they said someone would be out to remediate as soon as possible.

Comments: Arrived onsite for a routine inspection.There were 2 wells, 2 GPUs, 2 sand separators, 1 compressor, and 1 produced water tank onsite.The site was vegetated and appeared stable. There were no erosion or sedimentation issues noted. Infiltration areas were installed along the access road. The infiltration areas appeared to be functioning properly.There are outstanding violations as a result of puddles found on the pad surface that ranged from 3.18 to 5.44 milliSiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). These puddles were discovered on 3/21/23 (Inspection 3524618) near stockpiled material excavated from Chesapeake's Grippo pad. Additional violations were cited on 4/14/23 (Inspection 3537962) due to the receipt of analytical results from samples collected by DEP during the 3/21/23 inspection that confirmed the release of production fluid to the pad surface. Due to the unknown quantity of fluid, Chesapeake is performing remediation through Act 2.At the time of this inspection, soil and aqueous conductivity screening performed across the pad yielded results ranging from 0.03 to 0.13 mS/cm. No new violations noted, however, the result of this inspection is OUST for the following violations:78a64a(b), CSL 402(b) - Inspection 3524618 from 3/21/2378a66(b)1, 78a56(a), SWMA 301 - Inspection 3537962 from 4/14/23

Violation ID: 8277974
Permit API: 015-23981
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wysox Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/15/2026
Comments: On 02/26/2026 Expand representative Steven Moyer reported a discovered release onsite (CTS #395411). He stated "there was a hole in containment. An unknown amount of frack water mixed with stormwater on pad." On 02/27/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of the Wygrala Well Pad in Wysox Township, Bradford County. The area of the reported release is estimated to be an area of 75x150. Within the 75x150 area the elevated conductivity of the soil varies between 0-4 mS/cm. The cause of the release was due to a ripped seam in the pad wide containment.On 06/15/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of. The weather was 59 degrees and partly sunny. Rain fell on the pad within the last 24 hours. I arrived at 0900 hours. The site appeared stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation onsite. Pooled fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 505-892 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment. There was a water truck onsite during the inspection. There were six temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment. There were five wells capable of producing onsite. Each well was properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. Due to the unknown quantity of the release this has been referred to ECB for Act 2 compliance.Based on the reported release (CTS #395411) the following violations remain open against API #015-23981:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 0945 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-03-28 to Diversified Oil & Gas Llc in Fairfield Twp, Westmoreland county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Diversified Oil & Gas Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-03-28
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 845525
Permit API: 129-25936
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Fairfield Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-03-28
Comments: Inspection record #2860077 submitted on 3-28-19 was submitted in error. This inspection supersedes inspection record #2860077. At time of inspection well appears equipped for production. Department observes a thick, light yellow substance coming from brine tank. This substance appears to be petroleum based. This substance appears to be leaking from the top of the brine tank, where the piping from the well head attaches. This substance flows down the side of the brine tank (photo #1), and has ponded in two areas at the base of the brine tank (photo #2). Department contacted operator rep Josh Martz by phone from site. Mr. Martz states a well tender will be sent to the site. 14:42- Mr. Martz contacted Department by phone, left message. Mr. Martz states a release of approx 5-6 gal of crude oil occurred. Mr. Martz states water forced the tank to overflow. Mr. Martz states the tank has been emptied of water and that he will report the release to the DEP emergency line. 14:59- Department received spill report. This report states 5-6 gal of crude oil was released on 3-28-19. 16:32- Mr. Martz contacted Department by phone, left message. Mr. Martz states surface clean up has been completed. Mr. Martz states the crude oil will be removed from the tank next week. Mr. Martz states after crude oil is removed, the tank will be cleaned up, impacted soil will be removed, area under tank will be checked and impacted soil, if any, removed. Mr. Martz also states he will provide photos of cleanup to Department and will keep Department updated on status of site. Violations are being issued for failure to collect brine or other fluids, failure to control and dispose of fluids, and for disposal of residual waste inconsistent with the rules and regulations of DEP. A follow up inspection will be conducted at a later date.
